A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AugGen study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original face-recognition experiments, augmentation ablations, generative-metric comparisons and feature-space analyses in Section 4 and Appendices D–H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports training costs and unsuccessful StyleGAN-based training trials.

M1.justification: Equations 1–4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same generator training, mixed class conditions, similarity/dissimilarity search and augmentation procedure. Appendix C.2 explains generator choices without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CASIA-WebFace and WebFace160K, with additional real samples from WebFace4M, and evaluate on the same eight FR benchmarks. The newly described StyleGAN trials use the existing source datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports trying a StyleGAN-based generator on both source datasets and observing divergent training, adding a limited qualitative alternative-generator comparison. The scored FR comparisons retain DigiFace1M, RealDigiFace, IDiff-face, DCFace and the same real-data baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a comparison using training wall time and aggregate performance for IR50 trained on original or mixed data and IR101 trained on original data. Existing FR protocols, sample counts, grid-search settings and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an analysis of training cost versus backbone complexity and reports unsuccessful GAN training as evidence concerning generator choice. The existing mixing-amount, weighting, metric-correlation and feature-space analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C.6 introduces pooled standard deviations for its aggregate performance figures. The existing seed list and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. The added checklist mentions confidence intervals but supplies no new interval calculation or evidence of increased run counts.

E6.justification: All previously reported benchmark and ablation table values are retained. New Table 6 reports training times of 42.2 hours for the generator, 2.54 for IR50 on original data, 4.1 for IR50 on mixed data and 5.6 for IR101 on original data, alongside aggregates of existing performance results. StyleGAN training divergence is also newly reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and class-mixing formulation are unchanged. Appendix C.2 discusses ELBO objectives and flow matching through references to prior work, without introducing a new formal result, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain self-contained synthetic augmentation, improvements across eight FR benchmarks, gains competitive with architectural changes, approximately 1.7-times real-data equivalence and weak correlation with generative metrics. The revised title and abstract wording do not substantively alter these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds reasons for choosing diffusion models, including training maturity, observed GAN divergence and concerns about mode collapse on long-tailed data. Appendix C.6 argues that generator training overhead can be amortized through the smaller backbone's inference efficiency. Existing limitations and the impact statement are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 and Table 6 add training times tied to GPU configurations and IR101-to-IR50 FLOP and parameter ratios. These refine resource documentation without establishing changed training budgets. The hyperparameter table and promise of future public code, models and datasets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kingma and Gao's Understanding Diffusion Objectives as the ELBO with Simple Data Augmentation and Lipman et al.'s Flow Matching Guide and Code to support generator-choice discussion. The existing related-work coverage and central positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title now explicitly names diffusion models and recognition, with limited wording corrections elsewhere. Appendix C gains generator-choice and cost discussions, plus an empty Why Grid Search? subsection, and a NeurIPS checklist is inserted. The main narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 Figure 5 moves from Appendix A to the introduction as v3 Figure 2 with a shorter caption; the overview diagram also moves within the methodology. v3 adds Table 6 and reflows subsequent material. Existing figure imagery and benchmark-table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, Appendices C.2 and C.6 provide a more transparent account of generator choice and computational cost, helping readers assess practical feasibility while preserving the empirical evidence. The empty C.3 subsection and imprecise confidence-interval wording in the checklist limit polish. The net improvement is useful but modest.
